Doris K. Miller was an African American sailor in the United States Navy who served during World War II. He was born on October 12, 1919 in Waco, Texas. Miller enlisted in the Navy in 1939 and served as a Messman Third Class on the USS West Virginia.

On December 7, 1941, during the attack on Pearl Harbor, Miller showed great bravery and heroism. Despite not being trained in combat, he manned a machine gun and fired at Japanese aircraft, downing several enemy planes. Miller's actions were widely publicized and he became a symbol of heroism and patriotism for African Americans during a time of racial segregation in the military.

In 1942, Miller was awarded the Navy Cross for his actions at Pearl Harbor, making him the first African American to receive the honor. He continued to serve in the Navy and was later assigned to the USS Liscome Bay. Tragically, the ship was sunk by a Japanese submarine in November 1943 and Miller was one of the many sailors who lost their lives.

Doris K. Miller's legacy lives on as a pioneer and trailblazer for African Americans in the military. He is celebrated for his courage, bravery, and sacrifice in defense of his country. In 2020, the US Navy announced that a new aircraft carrier will be named in his honor, becoming the first carrier to be named after an African American.
